title: ⚔️ Chapter boss ⭐⭐⭐: reading the journey, measuring the time

questions.prompt: Read this club record, printed in the programme of a match played in 2026: "Club founded: 2004. First national title: 2009. In the first division without a break since: 2011. Present coach appointed: 2021." Which sentence about the club is right?

options.text: It has been playing in the first division for twenty-two years.
It is playing in the first division for fifteen years.
It has had the same coach for seventeen years.
It has been playing in the first division for fifteen years.

questions.explanation: "It has been playing in the first division for fifteen years." is right: the record says the club has been up there without a break since 2011, and from 2011 to 2026 is fifteen years, which for measures as a length. "It has been playing in the first division for twenty-two years." counts from 2004, but 2004 is the year the club was founded, not the year it went up. "It is playing in the first division for fifteen years." has the right number but opens with a present continuous, which describes this very moment and cannot stretch back to 2011. And "It has had the same coach for seventeen years." builds its figure on the first title, in 2009, whereas the present coach was appointed in 2021, five years before the match.

questions.prompt: Khaled, a coach from Gafsa, tells a school magazine: "I have been working with children for ten years now. I stopped playing in 2013, after a bad knee injury. Two years later I passed my coaching certificate, and the club offered me the junior team the following summer. I joined that same club as a player back in 2004." In which order did these four events happen?

options.text: joining the club as a player → the knee injury → the coaching certificate → the junior team
the knee injury → joining the club as a player → the coaching certificate → the junior team
joining the club as a player → the coaching certificate → the knee injury → the junior team
the coaching certificate → joining the club as a player → the knee injury → the junior team

questions.explanation: "joining the club as a player → the knee injury → the coaching certificate → the junior team" is the true order, and Khaled gives it out of order on purpose. He joined as a player in 2004, the earliest date of all, and he keeps that sentence for the very end of his story. The injury stopped him in 2013. Two years later means 2015 for the certificate, and the following summer means 2016 for the junior team — ten years before the interview, exactly what for ten years now announces. "the knee injury → joining the club as a player → …" and "the coaching certificate → joining the club as a player → …" both open on an event that already carries a later date, 2013 or 2015, and push the joining of the club down to second place, although 2004 is the earliest date on the page and nothing in the story happened before it. And "joining the club as a player → the coaching certificate → the knee injury → …" puts the certificate before the injury, whereas two years later counts from 2013 and therefore lands after it.

questions.prompt: Complete this note with the right pair of words: "Emna booked her ___ from Tunis to Djerba — fifty minutes in the air — and once there, she spent an afternoon watching a craftsman shape the silver ___ sold in the covered market."

options.text: excursion / leaflet
voyage / jewellery
flight / jewellery
flight / galleries

questions.explanation: "flight / jewellery" is the right pair: fifty minutes in the air can only be a flight, a journey by plane, and the silver rings and bracelets a craftsman shapes are jewellery. "voyage / jewellery" gets the second word right but calls the journey a voyage, which in English is a long journey by sea. "flight / galleries" gets the first word right and then puts galleries, the long rooms of a museum, in the place of the objects a craftsman produces. And "excursion / leaflet" is wrong twice over: an excursion is a short outing made for pleasure, usually by a group, not a seat you book from Tunis to Djerba, and a leaflet is a printed sheet, not something made in silver.

questions.prompt: A swimming teacher in Bizerte says two things about herself. (1) "I have taught six hundred children to swim." (2) "I have been teaching at this pool since 2009." Which question does sentence (1) answer?

options.text: How long have you been teaching at this pool?
How many children have you taught to swim?
When did you teach your first swimming lesson?
Why did you decide to teach children to swim?

questions.explanation: "How many children have you taught to swim?" is the question sentence (1) answers: a present perfect simple with a number in it counts finished results, and six hundred children is exactly such a count. "How long have you been teaching at this pool?" asks for a length of time, and that is what sentence (2) answers, with its progressive form and its starting point since 2009. "When did you teach your first swimming lesson?" asks for a date, and no present perfect can give one — the answer would have to be a past simple, I taught my first lesson in 2009. And "Why did you decide to teach children to swim?" asks for a reason, which neither of the two sentences gives.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, Hichem says: "I have been selling pottery in the same little shop in Nabeul for eleven years." A customer writes the story of the shop for a school magazine. Which sentence keeps Hichem's meaning?

options.text: I moved to Nabeul eleven years ago and left the shop in 2015.
I have been selling pottery in that little shop since 2015.
I have been selling pottery in that little shop since eleven years.
I sold pottery in that little shop for eleven years and then I left.

questions.explanation: "I have been selling pottery in that little shop since 2015." keeps the meaning whole: for measures the length, eleven years, and since names the point where that length begins — eleven years before June 2026, that point is 2015, and the tense keeps the shop open today. "I have been selling pottery in that little shop since eleven years." has the right idea but puts a length after since, which only accepts a point. "I moved to Nabeul eleven years ago and left the shop in 2015." contradicts itself, since 2015 is the very year Hichem arrived, and it closes a story that Hichem leaves open. And "I sold pottery in that little shop for eleven years and then I left." closes it too, with two past simples, whereas Hichem is still behind his counter.

questions.prompt: Mouna spent three weeks at a school camp in Bizerte last summer and came home with forty new friends. Her cousin Salma has just been invited to the same camp, but she is afraid of leaving home for so long. Which of Mouna's four replies gives Salma advice in correct English?

options.text: Why not to spend the first weekend with your cousin there?
You should to tell the teachers that you are afraid.
It is worth to phone home every single evening.
How about writing to one of the girls before you go?

questions.explanation: "How about writing to one of the girls before you go?" is the only reply that is correct English: how about is followed by a verb in -ing, never by an infinitive. "Why not to spend the first weekend with your cousin there?" adds a to that why not never takes, and the right shape is why not spend the first weekend with your cousin there. "You should to tell the teachers that you are afraid." puts to after a modal, whereas a modal is always followed by the bare verb: you should tell the teachers. And "It is worth to phone home every single evening." makes the same mistake after it is worth, which also calls for an -ing form: it is worth phoning home.
